Bug_Title: Methods should not call same-class methods with incompatible "@Transactional" values
Bug_Details:
Transactional methods have a propagation type parameter in the @Transaction annotation that specifies the requirements about the transactional
context in which the method can be called and how it creates, appends, or suspends an ongoing transaction.
When an instance that contains transactional methods is injected, Spring uses proxy objects to wrap these methods with the actual transaction
code.
However, if a transactional method is called from another method in the same class, the this argument is used as the receiver instance
instead of the injected proxy object, which bypasses the wrapper code. This results in specific transitions from one transactional method to another,
which are not allowed:
non- @Transactional
MANDATORY, NESTED, REQUIRED, REQUIRES_NEW
MANDATORY
NESTED, NEVER, NOT_SUPPORTED, REQUIRES_NEW
NESTED
NESTED, NEVER, NOT_SUPPORTED, REQUIRES_NEW
NEVER
MANDATORY, NESTED, REQUIRED, REQUIRES_NEW
NOT_SUPPORTED
MANDATORY, NESTED, REQUIRED, REQUIRES_NEW
REQUIRED or @Transactional
NESTED, NEVER, NOT_SUPPORTED, REQUIRES_NEW
REQUIRES_NEW
NESTED, NEVER, NOT_SUPPORTED, REQUIRES_NEW
SUPPORTS
MANDATORY, NESTED, NEVER, NOT_SUPPORTED, REQUIRED, REQUIRES_NEW
Bug_Explanation: The bug is that methods should not call same-class methods with incompatible '@Transactional' values. In this case, 'outerMethod' calls 'innerMethod', which is problematic if they had different transaction propagation settings, as the '@Transactional' annotation is missing here to demonstrate this issue.
Trigger_Explanation: The testShowBug method in the JUnit test is designed to call the showBug method of the TransactionalExample class. The showBug method, in turn, calls the outerMethod, which directly calls innerMethod without proper proxy handling due to the absence of '@Transactional' annotation on outerMethod. This internal call triggers the bug related to transactional propagation settings being incompatible.
